svg.title: Question-first method selection for the CREBAIN categorical MGW study
svg.desc: Publication diagram that separates four question-first lanes and sixteen typed method objects. Normalized innovation squared assesses per-channel innovation magnitude. Two-sided CUSUM is a separate operational diagnostic for sequential high- and low-direction innovation-magnitude change alarms. Signed Pearson correlation assesses directional linear agreement. None of these three operational diagnostics is evaluated by this fixture. KSG estimates general pairwise continuous dependence, including nonlinear dependence, when its declared support and row assumptions hold. Mutual information is direction-free with respect to correlation sign. KSG is not a PID. KSG is inapplicable to this repeated atomic categorical fixture. Categorical Makkeh-Gutknecht-Wibral shared-exclusions PID is produced because the study fixes ordered categorical sources, a named latent-truth target, and the complete empirical PMF. The primary PID2 chart uses a zero to 0.45 nat scale. This domain contains the largest value of 0.405465 nats. The chart shows informative, misinformative, and signed net components for redundancy, unique visual, unique radar, and synergy. The full eligibility matrix keeps the paper-defined categorical MGW functional separate from pid-core's budgeted PID2 and PID3 evaluators. It also keeps Williams-Beer I-min, two-source-only BROJA, the Schick-Poland general construction, the continuous Ehrlich functional, the Ehrlich nearest-neighbor estimator, pairwise KSG mutual information, co-information, O-information, normalized innovation squared, two-sided CUSUM, signed correlation, and the PNAS and ICLR infomorphic objective compositions separate. Only the MGW functional and its two selected pid-core evaluators produce output here. PID3 remains exploratory. It does not close the separate 108-coordinate averaged cumulative-plus-atom assurance program. The dependency-disjoint Decimal route compares 66 averaged atom components only. Asymmetric PID2 and PID3 canaries protect source order. All output remains record-only advisory evidence with no edge to FusedVerdict or Haldir policy.
svg.text: Choose the scientific object from the question—not from a method hierarchy
The four lanes are parallel. An unavailable object never triggers a fallback into a different estimand.
Two-sided CUSUM: high- and low-direction change alarms.
Separate diagnostics. Neither is evaluated by this fixture.
Did expected positive linear agreement change?
Direction is retained · common projection and lifecycle contract · operational lane
No correlation result is inferred from the PID fixture or from its favorable atoms.
Is an eligible continuous pair generally dependent?
General dependence, including nonlinear structure · direction-free · not PID
Repeated atomic rows violate this route. Added noise would change the estimand.
How is information about one target allocated?
Use a named PID functional on a fixed source–target estimand.
Here: categorical MGW · ordered sources · latent-truth target · empirical PMF
The output is a measure-relative statistical allocation, not a stronger verdict.
2 · PRIMARY PID2 RESULT · HORIZONTAL INCURSION · NATURAL-LOG UNITS
V = visual north-plane crossing · R = radar east-plane crossing · T_H = V ∧ R from synthetic latent ENU truth
MGW adds a target-specific allocation that
pairwise or joint association alone does not provide.
It does not establish causation, trust, attack intent,
fault responsibility, calibration, or permission to act.
Source order is protected by asymmetric PID2 and PID3
named-field canaries, not by symmetry or labels alone.
Pointwise values are retained but not independently compared.
Scale maximum = 0.45 nats. The largest bar, ln(3/2) = 0.405465…, is inside the plotted domain.
3 · SIXTEEN DISTINCT OBJECTS IN THE TYPED ELIGIBILITY MATRIX
Status applies only to this exact fixture. Functional, evaluator, estimator, diagnostic, and objective identities never transfer by proximity.

Sequential high- and low-direction innovation-magnitude alarms.

Two-input local learning goal composed from named atoms.

Role-distinct from the PNAS bivariate objective.
Outside this evaluator. It does not define another PID.
Reference roles are typed separately across MGW, Williams–Beer, Schick-Poland, Ehrlich, KSG, and co-/O-information.
Page (1954) supplies only the sequential CUSUM foundation. Harder–Rauh–Lyu supply caveats. Two papers define objectives.
Full author teams, titles, locators, and role boundaries are serialized in the study. Citation adjacency never authorizes method substitution.
No PID value enters FusedVerdict or a Haldir decision. Galadriel 0.9.0 has no Haldir adapter, runtime edge, or policy effect.
